text_content: davao flooding and the dutertes a balanced assessment an honest starting point flooding in davao is a legitimate concern that deserves serious attention some of the criticisms are grounded in real events including a genuine solid-waste crisis that cost lives this year at the same time much of the social-media commentary exaggerates the problem blurs who's actually responsible and paints this as a uniquely duterte-family failure a fair assessment holds both things at once real gaps and a national context that critics conveniently leave out national reality check flood control is a hard problem everywhere in the philippines outdated drainage garbage-choked waterways siltation and urbanization that outpaced 1970s-era infrastructure overwhelm every major city in heavy rain no lgu not manila not cebu not davao has a flood-free rainy season anyone claiming otherwise about any city is selling something davao carries the same systemic pressures as its peers but has put more visible work into the problem than most what has been delivered multiple drainage and flood-control projects since 2022 prioritized in high-risk districts including river rehabilitation on the matina bunawan and davao river systems seven dpwh pumping stations already operating across the city jerome mamay agdao marginal-to-magsaysay ponce roxas ext mabini ext plus two more in laverna with a third proposed city-funded drainage rehabilitation including php 35 million for the csc road drainage and php 40 million for the kabacan creek in ecoland residents in upgraded zones report noticeably faster water recession after heavy downpours compared to before these projects this is anecdotal rather than a published city metric but it's a consistent report worth taking seriously rather than dismissing rodrigo duterte's earlier line-item vetoes of questionable dpwh insertions reflected a genuine stance against pork-barrel-style spending which matters when we're talking about whether flood money gets spent honestly these are real verifiable steps not just promises where the record is genuinely weak and needs to be said plainly this is the part critics will hammer so let's not soften it on may 20 2026 a portion of the new carmen sanitary landfill collapsed after days of heavy rain killing at least one person and leaving others missing on top of injuries and displaced families denr suspended the landfill days later cited multiple violations of the ecological solid waste management act and permanently closed the old site in june that is not a maintenance footnote it was a fatal disaster and it happened on this administration's watch pretending otherwise would be dishonest beyond that incident the underlying problems are real and longstanding the landfill was already operating well past design capacity for years before it collapsed waste disposal roughly doubled from 2010 levels by 2025 and this was a known documented problem not a surprise drainage systems in several barangays have not received consistent desilting uncollected and improperly dumped garbage continues to clog canals and drainage inlets citywide and enforcement against illegal dumping and drainage encroachment remains inconsistent the new landfill and expansion projects were already underway before the collapse which shows the problem was recognized but recognizing a problem is not the same as having fixed it in time full transparency on the landfill collapse investigation and a public accounting of why the old site was allowed to run so far past capacity is the least residents deserve comparative perspective none of this erases the comparison that matters how does davao stack up against lgus facing the same pressures on project delivery and the resources actually put toward flood mitigation pumping stations river rehabilitation drainage funding davao has more to point to than many cities of similar size and budget that doesn't make davao's flooding acceptable it means the uniquely incompetent duterte fiefdom narrative pushed on social media doesn't survive contact with what other lgus are or aren't doing with comparable resources key clarifications the php 51 billion figure widely cited for rep paolo duterte's district 2020-2022 is routinely presented online as if it were all flood-control spending it wasn't dpwh-davao itself has clarified the figure later refined to php 49.8 billion covered the district's entire infrastructure portfolio roads bridges multipurpose buildings and major projects like the davao coastal road and bypass road dpwh's own breakdown puts the flood-control share at roughly php 9 billion a fraction of the total treating the full php 51b as a flood-control budget then pointing at continued flooding as proof the money didn't work is a category error not an accountability finding that said a real question remains open and shouldn't be waved away

text_content: davao the flood capital but perhaps not for the reason you think they say davao is the flood capital of the philippines well if someone insists on giving us that crown perhaps we should wear it proudly-but let's first ask a simple question what exactly is overflowing yes davao experiences floods we have rivers that swell after relentless rain low-lying communities that sometimes bear the brunt of nature sudden downpours that seem to arrive without an appointment and roads that occasionally transform into temporary swimming pools that is a real problem it deserves real solutions-not political theater but if we are going to compare cities perhaps the scoreboard deserves more than a political slogan during the severe southwest monsoon flooding in july 2025 for example the metropolitan manila development authority reported hundreds of flooding incidents across metro manila within a single day so before anyone points a finger at davao perhaps we should remember that flooding is not a problem exclusive to one city water does not check political affiliations before it rises rain does not ask who you voted for before it pours and rivers certainly don't read campaign speeches but here's where i see davao differently because there is another kind of flooding happening here-one that doesn't destroy homes close roads or leave mud behind davao floods with culture walk through this city and you encounter a living mosaic of mindanao indigenous traditions migrant communities different languages cuisines beliefs stories and histories woven together into one constantly evolving urban tapestry ask someone where they came from and you may discover an entire story behind the answer then inevitably there's food because in davao you can start a conversation about almost anything and somehow end up discussing durian this variety is sweeter no that one has better texture you haven't tried the best one yet suddenly what began as a casual conversation has transformed into an international conference on durian no registration fee required but perhaps davao's most remarkable flood is neither water nor culture it is warmth there is a quiet generosity in the character of many dabawenyos that statistics cannot measure you can arrive as a stranger and before long someone may already be telling you where to eat what places to visit which shortcut to take-and most importantly which road to avoid when traffic is terrible that's not just hospitality that's hospitality with a built-in traffic advisory and then there is davao's natural beauty the sea samal mount apo the forests the farms the rivers the mountains the wide spaces that remind you that progress and nature do not always have to be enemies davao is also changing businesses are arriving buildings are rising infrastructure is expanding communities are growing people continue to come-not only because they are looking for jobs but because they are looking for possibilities some arrive carrying résumés others arrive carrying business plans some arrive carrying nothing more than a dream and somewhere along the way many discover something unexpected they don't merely live in davao they become part of it that perhaps is the real story a city should not be judged solely by the problems that rise within it it should also be judged by what its people continue to build despite those problems davao is not perfect we have traffic we have growing pains we have environmental concerns we have infrastructure challenges we have political disagreements and of course we have social-media experts who can apparently repair the entire country using nothing but a smartphone and a facebook account but beneath all the noise is something far more difficult to construct character you can build a highway you can build skyscrapers you can build malls bridges offices and massive developments you can even build a spectacular roundabout that everyone will complain about for months but you cannot manufacture belonging you cannot pour it into concrete you cannot buy it from a catalog it has to grow and davao has grown through people people from different places came here they planted roots they built families they opened businesses they raised children they created communities and little by little their individual stories became part of the larger story of the city for the past 15 years i have had the privilege of traveling around davao for team-building activities retreats seminars workshops and speaking engagements and in those years i have seen something that no flood statistics can river in barangay gabu laoag city a project worth php 47,024,704.34 funded under the 2024 general appropriations act gaa has collapsed just months after its reported completion sparking fresh outrage over the alleged flood-control mafia operating in congress photos taken on-site show large concrete revetments cracked dislodged and washed into the river exposing reinforcing steel and leaving the riverbank vulnerable to further erosion the project billboard names ra pahati construction and supply inc as the contractor under the dpwh ilocos norte first district engineering office with a target completion date of october 4 2024 ra pahati construction is reportedly owned by the family of rep jhong ceniza of pantukan davao de oro a name that has repeatedly surfaced in infrastructure procurement circles sources familiar with congressional contracting allege that ra pahati has become a favored builder for rep sandro marcos the ilocos norte 1st district representative allegedly with some help from his chief of staff said to be a relative of rep ceniza's wife residents and local engineers have raised alarm over the collapse noting that the structure failed despite relatively moderate river flow in recent weeks infrastructure experts point out that proper soil compaction adequate riprap foundation and correct steel reinforcement are crucial in river dike construction all of which appear deficient in the broken sections the collapse has revived long-circulating allegations about flood control allocations being used as a cash cow for certain districts ra pahati controlled by the ceniza family has reportedly bagged billions in contracts across luzon and mindanao despite originating from davao de oro in ilocos norte whispers persist that rep sandro marcos chief of staff reportedly related by marriage to the cenizas has been instrumental in channeling projects to ra pahati bypassing stricter vetting political analysts warn this could become a serious governance issue for the presidential son especially as calls mount for greater transparency in the use of massive dpwh flood control budgets the incident adds to the growing backlash against multi-billion flood control projects nationwide long suspected to be overpriced poorly built and politically manipulated in congress several lawmakers particularly from mindanao have been calling out selective investigations that spare politically allied districts while targeting rivals observers warn that this laoag project could become a flashpoint especially since it sits in the home turf of text_content: congratulations davao city beyond traffic and rainy season how davao's coastal road is beating the floods davao coastal road flood control meets urban mobility yes davao city's coastal road isn't just a traffic reliever-it's a massive multi-purpose flood control and coastal protection project here's how it plays a vital role in flood resilience and urban development 1 storm-surge barrier and coastal defense designed as a coastal bypass the project doubles as a breakwater and shore protection system defending against sea wave actions storm surges and coastal erosion it incorporates hexapods seawalls grouted riprap and other shoreline defenses to reduce wave impact-a thoughtfully engineered coastline safeguard 2 integrated roadway and public spaces the 4 lane highway with asphalt pavement bike lanes pedestrian sidewalks and a 25.54 meter full-width design serves mobility recreation and safety purposes includes linear parks esplanades and promenades perfect for walking jogging or biking-offering both functional and leisure value 3 strategic flood resilience the elevated embankmented structure approx 6.5 meters on average complete with drainage frameworks helps mitigate flooding from coastal surges and heavy rains though technically it doesn't span rivers its design contributes indirectly to reducing flood impact in adjacent areas-especially during storm surges 4 complementing river flood control efforts meanwhile along the davao river dpwh is reinforcing revetment walls in baranguay mandug with structural sheet piles concrete capping and embankment fortification to control river flooding these efforts are nearing 90-94 percent completion and are slated for wrap-up by q4 2025 these projects operate synergistically-coastal road handling storm surge while river revetment mitigates overflow inland 5 timeline and scale the 17.8 km coastal road also called the coastal bypass road began in 2017 and is rolling out in phases with major segments already operational the iconic bucana bridge a 1.34 km p3.126 billion extradosed bridge linking coastal segments is under construction with completion expected by late 2025 full project completion is targeted between 2025 to 2026 with approximately php 28.5 billion already utilized and more funding pending for final works tugpaagilaprojectupdates king city of the south philippines text_content: when the waters rise in davao city so do the online critics following the heavy rains brought by the habagat and recent weather systems on july 24 2026 several neighborhoods across davao city once again faced rising floodwaters from mandug and tugbok down to low-lying areas like bangkal matina and talomo families had to endure another stressful night of monitoring river levels moving to higher ground or waiting for emergency teams and like clockwork as soon as photos of flooded streets flooded social media the comments section lit up with the usual outrage political potshots and online bashing where did the billions go why hasn't the city solved flooding yet it is completely understandable for affected residents to feel frustrated when water enters their homes but using these calamities to mock or tear down the city overlooks the actual science geography and non-stop work happening on the ground here is the perspective every dabawenyo and onlooker needs to hear 1 you cannot out-engineer a catch basin no politician regardless of their party and no amount of infrastructure spending can change basic topography davao city sits beside major river systems davao talomo matina lipadas bunawan and lasang flowing straight into the gulf key areas like bago gallera talomo proper ulas bangkal and matina are natural catch basins when continuous rains hit the highlands upstream millions of gallons of water naturally rush downward into these lower elevations add a high tide at the coast and the ocean acts like a giant dam preventing river mouths from discharging into the sea dikes and pumping stations can help manage overflow but they cannot stop gravity or push back the ocean 2 nature remembers its original shape parts of boulevard bucana agdao and sta ana were historically mudflats swamps and coastal wetlands humans can pave over these landscapes with roads subdivisions and concrete structures but when extreme rainfall happens water simply reclaims its natural pathways with climate change intensifying weather patterns nationwide rainfall volumes that used to happen once every few decades are now occurring multiple times a year this is a regional and global environmental challenge not an isolated municipal flaw 3 where did the funds go look at the defense systems in place critics often point to multi-billion flood control budgets as if money should make water instantly disappear but flood mitigation infrastructure isn't meant to stop rain from falling it's built to slow down water protect riverbanks and buy critical time pumping stations and retarding basins built in notorious bottlenecks like sasa and la verna to hold runoff and force water past high-tide barriers revetment walls and dikes miles of concrete dikes line the matina talomo and davao rivers to keep riverbanks from completely collapsing during sudden surges early warning and river monitoring the city disaster risk reduction and management office cdrrmo operates automated sensors and live hd monitoring cameras along all six major river channels allowing them to issue preemptive siren alarms and evacuation orders hours before water peaks 4 while keyboard warriors bash responders are out in the dark while critics type away in dry rooms hundreds of frontline responders from the cdrrmo bfp davao light urban search and rescue sar units and barangay disaster teams are out in waist-deep water executing rescue operations clearing clogged channels and moving stranded families to safety good governance in a coastal river-dense city isn't measured by the complete absence of natural calamities it's measured by preparedness quick response and zero casualties the fact that emergency teams can track upstream river swells in real-time and mobilize rescue trucks within minutes is proof of a functional disaster system bashing davao city during a flood won't lower the tide and weaponizing human suffering for online arguments won't stop the rain instead of tearing each other down let's focus on what actually keeps us safe community preparedness and cooperation when the cdrrmo issues a code red or sounds the warning siren do not wait follow evacuation protocols early look out for elderly neighbors keep your emergency kits ready and respect the responders risking their safety on the frontlines davao city has faced heavy weather before and we will always stand resilient through it stay safe stay vigilant and stay proud of our city daghang salamat sa atong responders

text_content: higher dike built along talomo river in davao city a higher dike has been completed along a portion of the talomo river in davao city with the project finished within just two months after public works secretary vince dizon ordered the immediate resumption and elevation of the river control structure the project was originally started in 2019 to help prevent severe flooding in communities located near the river the move followed president ferdinand marcos jr s directive to raise the structure by two meters on both sides of the river to help address flooding in the area the planned elevation of the dike was reportedly not pursued at the time allowing the river to overflow and affect nearby homes department of public works and highways

text_content: disclaimer this article is intended for my journalism class a million to one by kent sanchez millions suffer thousands die and only a few can ever get a taste of paradise beneath every struggle of a filipino with the frequent flooding there are those whose greed comes first before public service as the country struggles to cope with the aftermath of natural disasters davao is no stranger to these occurrences roads turn invisible dirty rainwater reaches knee-level and some end up in hospitals from diseases they never wished to become victims of 265 flood-prone areas were identified in davao city by the city engineer's office ceo most of which were also distinguished to be in district 1 according to david ezra m francisquete of sunstar davao due to these incidents christian a barangay rafael castillo lanang resident recalled a past experience with flooding in the area he explained how lanang is at risk of flooding incidents lanang is considered a coastal area because it sits right along the davao gulf a body of water on the southeastern coast of mindanao this means that when heavy rains coincide with high tide flooding is almost inevitable for homes near the shore he stated the lanang resident then added how these incidents happen so quickly that night the rain began lightly but quickly intensified within an hour canals in our subdivision and the main roads were soon submerged and within minutes raging waters started entering our home he expressed christian also that they resorted to evacuation as the flood had reached waist level until the next morning having their documents and valuables damaged our sofa much of our food some important documents and even our car were damaged by the flood it took us an entire week to clean repair and recover he said as the dpwh scandal arose he expressed how the mishandled flood control funds enraged him while countless filipinos continue to suffer from flash floods these officials choose to turn a blind eye and use public funds for their own gain christian stated he added that the discayas are not the only ones benefiting from these funds several politicians were also named by the discaya couple during the senate blue ribbon committee hearing as stated by giselle ombay of gma integrated news the secrets unravel and they are all pointing fingers but the question still remains-will there ever be change to the system the floods have become more frequent and so has corruption will the terrifying ratio of the fund allocation and the beneficiary always be a million to one photo credits to text_content: barangay sent 3 warning letters before callawa bridge 2 collapse pacc says davao city the presidential anti-corruption commission pacc has launched a formal investigation into the collapse of callawa bridge 2 after learning that the barangay council of callawa had allegedly sent at least three warning letters to the department of public works and highways dpwh before the structure gave way last week according to the pacc the letters raised serious concerns over visible cracks on the bridge severe erosion beneath the structure exposed bridge foundations and posts and the possibility that the bridge could collapse during heavy flooding residents and barangay officials claimed the warnings were repeatedly brought to the attention of authorities but were allegedly never properly acted upon the bridge collapsed on may 18 following continuous heavy rains triggered by the intertropical convergence zone itcz and easterlies disrupting transportation access and affecting residents and motorists in barangay callawa and nearby communities during an ocular inspection conducted friday pacc officials and volunteer engineers observed extensive erosion and scouring along the bridge approaches with large portions of supporting soil already washed away by strong floodwaters pacc chairman dr louie f ceniza said the incident raises serious concerns about accountability and public safety if prior warnings were indeed raised by the barangay council and residents these concerns should have been immediately addressed before the situation escalated into a disaster ceniza said the people deserve answers the public deserves accountability he added the inspection was conducted in the presence of pacc bot member rev richie cubos dpwh davao city 3rd district engineering office assistant district engineer andrew pangan and volunteer civil engineers from davao city assisting in the initial technical assessment the collapsed structure forms part of the dpwh region xi infrastructure project identified as project id no 17l00133 covering the concreting widening and improvement of the buhangin-tigatto-mandug-callawa-fatima road including reconstruction of callawa bridge the project implemented by dpwh region xi and undertaken by contractor premium megastructures inc cost p190.7 million and was completed in december 2018 initial observations by the pacc indicated that the bridge may have lacked sufficient upstream and downstream flood protection measures investigators said approximately 100 meters of flood control protection on both sides of the bridge could have minimized or prevented the erosion that undermined the structure the pacc also noted the collapse of nearby utility poles due to severe soil erosion and loss of support as part of the probe the commission said it will review approved engineering plans hydraulic and geotechnical studies construction quality control reports inspection and acceptance records maintenance documents and all correspondence submitted by barangay callawa including dpwh responses to the reported concerns pacc bot member and spiritual adviser bishop rod cubos said the incident highlights the consequences of negligence and inaction this incident reminds us that negligence and indifference can lead to suffering danger and hardship within our communities cubos said the pacc emphasized that findings from the inspection remain subject to further technical validation and documentary review meanwhile the commission acknowledged the ongoing efforts of the dpwh davao city 3rd district engineering office headed by ade engr andrew pangan which is currently supervising the construction of a temporary bridge to restore access for affected communities we we
